Good evening, Chair Seberg, Vice Chair Spall, Dr. Newman, and members of the board. I am happy to provide a September construction update on the new Jenny Dean Elementary School project. First, I'm happy to report that the product remains on schedule and on budget.

Our contractor and our partner, Shockey and Sons, continues to staff the site with approximately 100 workers each day, keeping their progress steady and on track. During September, we saw significant advancement in site work, particularly with the installation of the underground stormwater retention system.

The contractor also has modified the sequence of the disciplines, which allowed us to make the other trades be able to continue their work uninterrupted. In addition to the site, the site grading and backfilling progressed on plan, and all of the environmental compliance inspections were completed with no deficiencies, which is great news.

Inside the building footprint, crews have made good progress on the structure. The roof joists were installed at the stair towers and at the gym, and the roof decking continued across major areas of the building. The masonry work advanced on the first and second grade classroom wings, and the mechanical, electrical, and plumbing rough-ins were moved forward in areas now protected by the roof structure.

Once the decking is fully in place, the roofing operations will begin, and this puts us on track for enclosure milestones before the winter. Our goal is to get the building enclosed before the winter months so that work can continue inside the building, and we're on track to do that.

I also want to highlight the continued strong coordination among the contractor, our architects, our engineers, and our inspection teams. The questions and field issues are being resolved very quickly, which has kept the workflow smooth and uninterrupted.

Just as importantly, the contractor continues to be a great partner for us and has a great existing relationship with the current Jenny Dean Elementary School. So learning there has had minimal disruption, which we greatly appreciate on our side.

So overall, the project continues to move forward with momentum, with discipline and clear alignment to our schedule. And as I said at the beginning, we remain on track and the next major focus will begin moving the building toward full enclosure as the roofing and masonry can continue before the winter months.

From the very beginning, the design of the Jenny Dean Elementary School was never about the building alone. It was about our children, it was about learning, about community, and about history. This creates a real-world learning opportunity tied directly to the Virginia Standards of Learning for science, specifically the water cycle. So for example, in grade three science, SOL standard 3.7 says that students must understand and will investigate the water cycle, understand evaporation, condensation, precipitation. The standard says that students will investigate and understand that there is a water cycle and that water is important to life on earth. In grade four,

students investigate Virginia watersheds. As part of the curriculum in the SOL standards 4.8a, students are expected to use evidence to explain the statement, we all live downstream. So instead of only reading about the water cycle and watersheds in a textbook, our students will be able to observe stormwater being collected, stored, and released in real time. They will see water flowing toward the collection pond and teachers will be able to connect these observations to vocabulary such as precipitation and watershed. This makes the abstract
